memory_candidates.content: In this repo, extension-provided scripts deploy FLAT into .claude/scripts/ regardless of which extension's source store they originate from (manifest.json provides.scripts arrays are flat basename lists). So two scripts from different source-store extensions (e.g. agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lake-build-guard.sh and agent-system/extensions/lean/scripts/lean-sorry-census.sh) become siblings only post-deploy, not in the source tree. A script that wants to invoke a sibling deployed script robustly should use a dirname-relative lookup ($(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/other-script.sh) defaulted via an overridable env var (e.g. FOO_OTHER_SCRIPT_BIN), mirroring the LAKE_BUILD_GUARD_LAKE_BIN test-seam precedent in lake-build-guard.sh, so tests running directly against the source store (where the sibling lookup would fail) can inject a fixture.

Extension lifecycle hooks (skill_run_extension_hook in skill-base.sh) resolve strictly on the CURRENT TASK's task_type via skill_get_extension_dir, not on which files the task touches. A meta- or general-typed task that edits files belonging to a domain extension (e.g. lean) will never trigger that extension's preflight/context_injection hook, even though the edited files are squarely in that extension's domain. This is a structural coverage gap worth checking before proposing a hook as an enforcement mechanism for cross-cutting concerns.
